# The design tokens

The tokens under the compatibility floor: the ones an extension may rely on, and the ones that may be read live.

Read from the source: every name below, its signature, its JSDoc, and — for a type or a class — its own members.

| Name | Kind | Defined in | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`PUBLISHED_TOKENS`](#published-tokens) | const | `tokens.ts` | Published tokens, by what they are for. |
| [`TOKEN_NAMES`](#token-names) | const | `tokens.ts` | Every published token name, flat. |
| [`ThemeTokens`](#themetokens) | type | `tokens.ts` | Token name → current value. |
| [`readThemeTokens`](#readthemetokens) | function | `tokens.ts` | Read the published tokens as they are right now. |
| [`applyThemeTokens`](#applythemetokens) | function | `tokens.ts` | Apply tokens inside the extension's own document. |

## PUBLISHED_TOKENS

```typescript
const PUBLISHED_TOKENS
```

Published tokens, by what they are for.

Grouped because the groups are how an author reads them: pick a
surface, pick the text that goes on it, pick a tone for the
meaning. Names match the app's own so a reader moving between the
two is not translating.

## TOKEN_NAMES

```typescript
const TOKEN_NAMES: readonly string[]
```

Every published token name, flat.

Derived rather than listed. A second list would be a second place
to forget — and the groups above are an object literal, where a
repeated key silently keeps only the last one. That happened: the
type scale was added as `text`, which was already the foreground
colours, and `--fg` disappeared without a word.

## ThemeTokens

```typescript
type ThemeTokens = Record<string, string>
```

Token name → current value.

## readThemeTokens

```typescript
function readThemeTokens(root: Element = document.documentElement,): ThemeTokens
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | `Element` | `document.documentElement` | the element whose computed styles are read; the document's own root by default. |

Read the published tokens as they are right now.

Computed values, not declared ones: a token defined in a media
query or overridden by a `data-theme` attribute resolves here to
what the user is actually looking at, which is the only answer
worth sending.

**Also** [`ThemeTokens`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-design-tokens#themetokens).

## applyThemeTokens

```typescript
function applyThemeTokens(tokens: ThemeTokens, root: HTMLElement): void
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tokens` | `ThemeTokens` | required | what to apply: each published name and the value it takes. |
| `root` | `HTMLElement` | required | the element they are applied to. |

Apply tokens inside the extension's own document.

Called by the guest bridge. Separate from reading them so the two
halves can be tested without a frame between them.

**Also** [`ThemeTokens`](/docs/sdk/extension-bridge/reference-the-design-tokens#themetokens).
